summary: Skull and Crossbones ridge lookout near Loomis WA: a ground L-4 cab built 1932, sold and helicopter-moved to Horseshoe Basin in 1953; remains on the ridge, cab's fate unknown.

facts.status_note: The ridge site has no cab; the cab was sold in 1953 and moved by helicopter to Horseshoe Basin, where WillhiteWeb records its fate as unknown; wall, stove parts and cans remain on the ridge

access.note: Original site reached by a roughly 20-mile approach through the Loomis State Forest on roads that change, get abandoned and wash out. Sources name no gate or permit. Level inferred from the route description, not from an agency notice

visit.trail_note: About 20 miles of approach roads through Loomis State Forest; final road abandoned and not drivable near the top; WillhiteWeb says hiking from the base adds only about 1.5 miles. Horseshoe Basin is within the Pasayten Wilderness

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Okanogan National Forest, per registry and firelookout.com); the registry, firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb also place the site in the Loomis State Forest

events.note: Ground L-4 cab constructed in 1932; an August 1932 Wenatchee newspaper item reported several lookout houses finished, including one above Loomis
Dick Loudon was the lookout; he went to a forest training camp in June 1933
M.F. Gadberry named as lookout for 1934; panoramic images taken from the roof at 15 feet above ground
M.F. Gadberry again at the lookout in 1935
Cab sold and moved by helicopter to Horseshoe Basin for Emmit Smith's cattle grazing permit
Photo on the relocated-cab page captioned as showing the cab in 1956
Smith permit continued when the eastern part of the North Cascades Primitive Area became the Pasayten Wilderness
Photo on the relocated-cab page captioned as Emmet at the cab in 1969
Registered November 19, 2012 as FFLOS US 1466, WA 366; nominated by Ray Kresek

corrections.why: The cab was sold and moved by helicopter to Horseshoe Basin in 1953, so it was moved rather than destroyed on site. Its fate after that is unknown. 'Gone' fits the ridge site only.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The registry and firelookout.com both name the Okanogan National Forest, yet both also describe the site as in the Loomis State Forest, as does WillhiteWeb. The story reports both names and does not choose between them.

sources.title: Skull and Crossbones Fire Lookout Cabin

notes_for_editor: Two-part record: the ridge site (no cab since 1953) and the relocated cab in Horseshoe Basin, whose fate is unknown per WillhiteWeb (cite 5), so the story covers both. Horseshoe Basin is in the Pasayten Wilderness; the story does not suggest a visit there. Landowner conflict flagged (Okanogan NF vs Loomis State Forest). The WillhiteWeb ridge photos are undated, so 'still standing' is as of an undated visit. Not used: a WebSearch snippet giving 5,964 ft for a 'Skull and Crossbones Cabin' topo entry, and a trail-guide mention of old cabin remnants on the ridge, neither verified on a page. The 'Purchased August 8, 1953' line on the ridge page is a photo caption and was not used.
